checks.name: CONTACTS
checks.evidence: Using seed 31 and real Chromium mouse input, a single opening click cut once and sharply anchored on white-landing at 1.496 s wall time. Repeating the opening with only one simple timing change—a second click at 450 ms—cut once and produced a visible blunt bounce at 0.816 s. contact-anchor.png and contact-450.png show the distinct branches; the bounce branch remained airborne and recoverable.

checks.name: BONUS
checks.evidence: The same visible-state real-input route split reliably near the finish: a correction at x≈2609 selected safe and won at 15.387 s, while moving that correction slightly earlier to x≈2506 selected bonus and entered the visibly distinct purple bonus course at 16.194 s. A real click in bonus produced a cut, then no further correction caused fall failure after 2.607 s. One terminal real click returned to phase=ordinary/status=ready, proving the failed bonus chance did not restart in bonus.

checks.name: RUNTIME
checks.evidence: During active mid-course flight, a 1.394 s main-thread stall plus observation overhead measured 1.645 s wall time and advanced simulation by 1.592 s. The blade remained airborne and progressed from x=686.1 to x=963.05, so accumulated active time was not silently truncated.

checks.name: MOBILE
checks.evidence: At 390x844, native touch produced launch, first cut and anchor on white-landing. A separate native-touch cadence reached spike failure, and one native terminal touch returned to ordinary/ready with failReason cleared. scrollWidth/innerWidth and scrollHeight/innerHeight were exactly 390/390 and 844/844 with scrollX=scrollY=0.

checks.name: ERRORS
checks.evidence: Desktop and mobile Chromium sessions recorded zero page errors and zero console errors. Only Chromium WebGL ReadPixels performance warnings appeared; no game exception or failed runtime request was observed.
